facts.text: In 1842 the Michigan Central Railroad bypassed Grass Lake’s original village, building a depot 1.5 miles west after a $1.50‑per‑acre offer.
Founded in 1971, the Grass Lake Area Historical Society preserves local history and operates the Coe House Museum, a 1870s home turned exhibit space.
The Coe House Museum opened in 1972 after the society purchased Myrta Coe’s former home, transforming it into a public museum.
A self‑guided historic walking tour loops through downtown Grass Lake, highlighting landmarks and stories that bring the village’s past to life.
In 1971 Grass Lake celebrated its centennial, prompting the community to dedicate a historic home as a museum to honor its heritage.
